newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TEXAS BUSINESSMAN AGREES TO BUY THE ISLANDERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TEXAS BUSINESSMAN AGREES TO BUY THE ISLANDERS.

text.p: Texas businessman John Spano reached final agreement Tuesday to buy 90 per cent of the New York Islanders for $165 million and said he will not move the hockey team.
"Yes, the Islanders will stay here," said Spano, a native New Yorker who is the chairman of The Bison Group, an aircraft and heavy equipment firm in Dallas. "Yes, the fans deserve a new arena."
"The goal of this new ownership group will be to build the next generation of champions," Spano said. "Every decision we make will be based on one question: What is best for hockey?"
Spano takes over from John Pickett, who has owned the team since 1978.
The sale of any team is subject to the approval of the 26-member NHL Board of Governors. The next meeting of the Board is scheduled for December 12th and 13th in Phoenix.
